result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.incremental_closeness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Get the closeness centrality the graph would have after adding or removing one edge. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.incremental_closeness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Get the closeness centrality the graph would have after adding or removing one edge. title: >- [Graph.incremental_closeness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Get the closeness centrality the graph would have after adding or removing one edge. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the closeness centrality the graph would have after adding or removing one edge. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46865-L46966){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.incremental_closeness_centrality( edge, prev_cc=None, insertion=True, wf_improved=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Incremental closeness centrality](../assets/graphs/incremental-closeness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node path 1 to 6 drawn as a ring, with the edge e = (1, 6) that would close it dashed; cc, the current closeness scores, is passed in. Nodes 1, 2, 5 and 6 (accent) are at least two hops closer to one end of the new edge than the other, so their closeness is recomputed; nodes 3 and 4 are not, and keep their previous score. The table gives each node's score before and after: 1 and 6 rise from 0.33 to 0.56, 2 and 5 from 0.45 to 0.56, and 3 and 4 stay at 0.56. The graph itself is not changed." width="100%"} A "what if" for closeness: the scores are those of the graph with `edge` added (or, with `insertion=False`, with it removed), but the graph itself is not changed. Given the current scores as `prev_cc=`, only the nodes whose distances can change are recomputed, which is much faster than a fresh `closeness_centrality()` when the edge affects only part of the graph. This makes it suited to trying many candidate edges in turn, for example to find the new link that brings a node closest to everyone, or the road closure that hurts access the least. Distances are hop counts (weights are ignored), so `prev_cc=` should come from `closeness_centrality(weighted=False, return_dict=True)` with the same `wf_improved=`; scores computed some other way are copied into the result unchecked. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edge to add or remove, as a pair of node IDs or labels. [prev_cc]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The closeness scores of the graph as it is now, one per node. If `None` (default), every score is computed from scratch. [insertion]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), score the graph with `edge` added (a parallel copy, if the nodes are already joined). If `False`, score it with one copy of `edge` removed. [wf_improved]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to scale each score by the fraction of other nodes it can reach (the Wasserman-Faust correction), as in `closeness_centrality()`. Default `True`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID to closeness score in the changed graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, a node does not exist, `insertion=False` and the nodes are not joined by an edge, or `prev_cc=` does not have exactly the graph's nodes. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~closeness_centrality`) : Closeness centrality of the graph as it is. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Adding an edge `u`-`v` can only shorten paths that use it. A node `x` whose distances to `u` and `v` differ by at most one gains nothing from the new edge, since going through it is never shorter than the way `x` already reaches the farther end, so `x` keeps its score (Kas, Carley and Carley, 2013). This needs a breadth-first search from `u` and from `v` in the graph without the edge (before an insertion, after a removal), then one more for each node that fails the test. Matches NetworkX's `incremental_closeness_centrality`. NetworkX adds or removes the edge temporarily and, when `prev_cc` is not given, leaves the graph changed; EdgeCase never changes the graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Closing a six-node path into a ring: ::: {#5ec142c9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(6) before = g.closeness_centrality(weighted=False, return_dict=True) after = g.incremental_closeness_centrality((1, 6), prev_cc=before) {node: (round(before[node], 3), round(after[node], 3)) for node in sorted(after)} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: (0.333, 0.556), 2: (0.455, 0.556), 3: (0.556, 0.556), 4: (0.556, 0.556), 5: (0.455, 0.556), 6: (0.333, 0.556)} ``` ::: ::: Nodes 3 and 4 sit in the middle, two hops from one end and three from the other, so the new edge shortens none of their paths: their scores were copied from `before` rather than recomputed. The graph itself is still a path: ::: {#bd8e3ab0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
